pathways.climate_pressure: Coastal flooding, salinity and source-described sea-level pressure around Djobel.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to rice-field/dike systems and pressure to establish safer settlement space.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Longstanding contested upland access, unresolved resource rights, limited support and labour constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: The case documents obstacles to safer settlement/adaptation and renewed land tensions; it does not isolate climate change as the origin of the dispute.
alternative_explanations: Longstanding territorial history, state action, resource rights, livelihood dependence and external assistance also shape adaptation and tensions.
pathways.uncertainty: Localized historical qualitative evidence; no attribution of the 2017 flood to anthropogenic change, quantified violence trend, or present land adjudication.
resilience_factors: Equitable negotiated access, dike maintenance and appropriate technical support are relevant capacities; effectiveness is not established.
pathways.compact_statement: In Djobel, flood exposure and pressure to retreat interact with an older upland land dispute that constrains safer settlement; the case is local and multi-causal.

executive_assessment.text: Djobel adds a detailed historical flood, dike, mobility and contested safer-land case; it cannot represent Guinea-Bissau as a whole.
Hydromet projects face financial and political constraints, while WFP service and resilience commitments remain separately dated plans/capacity context.
